claims.claim: Rodriguez had recognized her potential in Sin City and Planet Terror
claims.note: Interview: Rodriguez "has identified this potential in me, both in Sin City and Planet Terror". Body keeps this wording.

claims.claim: Rodriguez writes, directs, DPs, scores, edits and mixes his own movies
claims.note: Interview: "writes, directs, DPs, scores, edits and mixes his own movies".

claims.claim: Dakota modelled on Hitchcock ice-queen blondes; she studied suspense
claims.note: Interview: "I modeled my character Dakota off of the old Hitchcock, ice queen blondes." and "I have studied suspense".

claims.claim: Her favorite Hitchcock film is Psycho; she likes Dial M for Murder
claims.note: Asked for her favourite Hitchcock film, answer "Psycho." Dial M: "I just watch Dial M for Murder; I hadn't seen it in ages."

claims.claim: Rodriguez asked her to play one sequence as if from a silent movie
claims.note: Interview: "Robert directed me to play this scene as if it was from a silent movie."

claims.claim: Planet Terror shot first, Death Proof second, all at Troublemaker Studios in Austin
claims.note: Interview: "We shot Planet Terror first, then we shot Death Proof." and "We shot everything at Troublemaker Studios". Crew clause removed.

claims.claim: Tarantino on set for Planet Terror and helped co-direct it
claims.note: Interview: "Quentin was on set the whole time" and "He really helped in co-directing the movie."

claims.claim: Running in high heels; stunt double Tracey Dashnaw did the window jump
claims.note: Interview: "running in high heels night after night"; "Tracey Dashnaw ... She did the scene of Dakota jumping out the window".

claims.claim: Rodriguez digital and quick; Tarantino shot on film and was the more verbal director
claims.note: Interview: Tarantino "prefers to shoot on film", "much more verbal director"; Rodriguez "extremely cutting edge" with technology. The word 'digital' is not quoted; read as the contrast with film.

claims.claim: Rodriguez called Planet Terror a Gore-Ball comedy blending screwball comedy with zombies
claims.note: Interview: "he decided to marry the two into what he dubbed 'Gore-Ball' comedy".

claims.claim: The Fifth Patient (2007), expected to screen at CineVegas
claims.note: Interview: "it will be playing at CineVegas"; TMDb The Fifth Patient 2007 (Helen).

valueNote: Dated timeline built on TMDb, Wikidata, Brave Beginnings, BroadwayWorld and the 2007 and 2022 interviews. German text is written for German readers. The unsupported Rodriguez, crew, Tarantino and E! framing sentences were fixed to what the sources say.
summary: Approved after fixes: Rodriguez quotes now match the Grindhouse interview; crew clause dropped; Tarantino line matches the source; E! framing reattributed to the article; Psycho answer narrowed to favourite Hitchcock film.
